p: Chapter 1 · What payroll is, and why it is hard
x: Payroll is the work an employer does every pay period to pay its employees: compute each one's pay from the contract and the time worked, pay the net to the employee, and pass the amounts it kept back on to the authorities, with the reports that prove them. The word also names the list of employees and amounts for one period (the October payroll). Other names: payroll processing, salary administration, pay run. Three things follow from that definition: It never stops. The same computation runs every period for every employee, with new inputs each time: a hire, a sick day, a rate that changes in July. Much of the money is not the employee's to keep. Part of the salary goes to social security and to the tax office; the employer collects it and is liable for it (next section, and Chapter 2). Someone checks it. The authorities receive the money and the reports on their own calendar, and can recompute any payslip. Illustrative calendar. Every month the payroll is computed and the net is paid. The tax withheld is filed and paid the next month, the contributions after each quarter, a certificate per employee after the year, and a hire or an exit is notified when it happens. Dates differ by country; the four clocks are almost universal.

p: Chapter 1 · What payroll is, and why it is hard
x: In every country, payroll moves money from one payer to several receivers. The names change; the shape does not. Employer the only payer computes every payslip keeps back tax and contributions pays everyone declares it all, and is liable if it is wrong pays the total employer cost net pay Employee the net pay, on their bank account for the work done; what is left after deductions contributions Social security the employee’s and the employer’s contributions one fund or many; finances pensions, health, unemployment tax withheld Tax authority the income tax withheld from the employee an advance on the employee’s yearly tax, with the returns that prove it their share Third parties pension funds, meal-voucher issuers, a court-ordered creditor money the contract or a court sends elsewhere The bank only carries the transfers. A payroll provider, if the company uses one, computes and files on its behalf, but the employer stays responsible. Key idea The employer is an unpaid collection agent for the state: it deducts, pays and reports for the employee, and is liable if it does not. In many countries, Belgium included, a contribution the employer forgot to deduct cannot be claimed back from the worker later.3

x: Three properties make payroll unforgiving, in every country. It is law, not preference. A forgotten hire notice is a criminal offence in Belgium.6 It cannot be undone once paid. You correct on a later payslip (Chapter 6). It is checked from outside. The authorities cross-check returns, payments, yearly certificates and the employee's own tax return.

p: Chapter 1 · What payroll is, and why it is hard
h: Rules that move during the year
x: A payroll rule is a value with a start date. Most countries change rates and tax tables on 1 January; many also change something mid-year. Belgium changed its withholding formula on 1 January and again on 1 November 2026.9 With the same gross, the November change lowers Mélanie's, Jurgen's and Yannick's withholding by 8.47 € a month but raises Marie's by 28.86 €: the new formula gives less relief to a married couple with one income.1 Chapter 4 explains why; Chapter 11 shows how Odoo stores both formulas. Worked example: what a forgotten update costs Keep the January formula in November: Mélanie, Jurgen and Yannick are over-withheld 8.47 € a month and get it back a year later; Marie is under-withheld 28.86 € a month and pays at her assessment. Neither error shows on the day, and every monthly return is wrong until the fix. Common pitfall Treating payroll as "salary minus a few percentages". The percentages come with caps, low-wage reductions, family relief, special bonus rates and effective dates. Each is a bug waiting in a naive implementation; the next seven chapters take them one at a time. In practice Odoo customers often still use an accountant or payroll bureau for some filings. When you scope a project, ask early: who files the social security return, who files the tax return, who pays the net?

HR, social security and the tax office all say "salary" and mean different amounts. Confusing them is the most common design bug in payroll software.

p: Chapter 2 · Gross to net
h: What gross and net pay are
x: Gross pay (gross salary, gross wage) is what the employee earns for the period before anything is taken off: the contract salary plus any other earnings. Net pay (take-home pay) is what reaches the employee's bank account, after the employee's contributions, the withholding tax and any other deductions. The calculation from one to the other is called gross to net, and the payslip is its written record. Three things follow from that definition: Gross is not what the company pays. The employer adds its own contributions on top of the gross. They never touch the net: they are a cost on top of the salary, and the two together are the employer cost. The gap between gross and net is the employee's money. The employee contributions and the withholding tax are kept back by the employer and passed on to the authorities: the employer is only a collector. "Salary" is ambiguous. Gross, net, and the bases on which contributions and tax are computed are different numbers. This chapter computes each one. Whatever the country, one month of salary is one pot of money, paid by the employer and split three ways. Illustrative numbers, to scale: What the company pays1,200employer cost Gross salary1,000 Employer contributions200 What it becomes Net pay650 Withholding tax200 Employee contrib.150 Employer contrib.200 ← the gross: 1,000, all of it earned by the employee →on top of gross Who receives it Employee's bank650 Tax authority200 Social security350150 employee + 200 employer Top bar: the employer cost. Middle bar: the gross splits into the net and the employee's deductions, with the employer contributions beside it. Bottom bar: the authorities receive the tax and both halves of the contributions. The shape is the same in every country; what changes is the number of recipients and whether the tax segment exists. Hong Kong is the clearest contrast: the employer withholds no income tax. It reports each employee's yearly pay to the tax office, which assesses the tax and collects it from the employee directly (the one exception: an employee leaving Hong Kong for good, whose final payment the employer must hold back). The only mandatory contribution is the pension fund, 5 % from each side. Illustrative numbers again: What the company pays1,050employer cost Gross salary1,000 Employer pension50 What it becomes Net pay950 Employee pension50 Employer pension50 Who receives it Employee's bank950 Pension fund10050 employee + 50 employer Not to scale: the pension boxes are enlarged so their numbers fit. No tax segment: nothing goes to the tax authority. Around the world Australia: no employee contribution at all; the employer pays superannuation into the employee's pension fund. United States, India: several recipients instead of one social security office (federal and state tax; separate pension and health funds). United Arab Emirates: no income tax; a pension contribution for nationals only. Employer cost = Gross + employer contributions Taxable base = Gross − employee contributions + benefits in kind Net = Gross − employee contributions − withholding tax − other deductions Benefits in kind are not paid in cash: they only raise the taxable base, and so the tax.

p: Chapter 2 · Gross to net
x: Every earning on a payslip has to answer two questions, because two different laws look at it: social-security law decides what contributions are taken from, tax law decides what is taxed. They often agree, but not always. Does social security take its share? Is it in the contribution base? Is it taxed? Is it in the taxable base, and at which rate? Two yes-or-no answers give four boxes, and every earning falls into one of them: Taxed Not taxed Social security takes its share The usual case base salary, overtime, allowances bonuses and 13th month, often at a special tax rate MyVidangeCompany: everyone's salary Rare pay set aside in a US 401(k) retirement plan: social security still applies, income tax is deferred No social security Taxed only benefits in kind, valued by a legal formula, where the law exempts them from contributions: a company car in Belgium (other countries also take contributions on them) MyVidangeCompany: Marie's car Neither meal vouchers, within the legal limits expense reimbursements that repay a real cost MyVidangeCompany: Marie's meal vouchers The same earning can sit in a different box in another country, which is why a localization answers both questions for every earning it ships. Key idea Design each earning with both answers, stored on the rule. A Belgian company car is taxable but not subject to contributions. An "is it taxable?" flag alone is never enough. Around the world Saudi Arabia, UAE: salary = basic + housing + transport, each fixed on the contract. Switzerland: a catalogue of numbered wage types, each a salary rule. India: the salary is split into components (basic, house rent, travel…) on the contract. Kenya, Philippines, Mexico: some allowances and vouchers are exempt up to a cap; the excess is taxable. United States: pre-tax benefits (retirement, medical) lower the taxable base.

h: Benefits in kind: Marie's company car
x: A benefit in kind is pay that never touches a bank account. The law values it with a formula, and payroll adds the value to the taxable base. In Belgium, a car's yearly benefit is catalogue value × age coefficient × 6/7 × a CO2 percentage (4 % for an electric car), with a minimum of 1,690.00 € in 2026.4 Worked example: Marie's electric SUV Catalogue value 52,000.00 €, first registered on 5 January 2026 (age coefficient 100 %), 0 g CO2/km. Step Amount (€) 52,000.00 × 6/7 × 4 % × 100 % 1,782.86 per year Minimum for 2026 1,690.00 per year ATN.CAR Benefit retained, per month 148.57 The benefit goes into Marie's taxable base, not her contribution base; instead the employer pays a monthly CO2 contribution of 42.34 €.5 In Odoo. Odoo spreads the same yearly benefit by days instead of twelfths: 151.42 € in October (31/365), not 148.57 €. The year adds up the same.1

Example at MyVidangeCompany Compulsory employee contributions yes, in most countries employee social security, 13.07 % Pre-tax benefits (pension, medical) yes, where the law allows — Other contributions after tax no special social security contribution Employee share of a benefit, garnishment no meal-voucher employee part Order matters because each rule reads totals computed before it: the tax needs the contributions; a garnishment ceiling needs the net. p: Chapter 2 · Gross to net
x: Every contribution and every tax is a percentage of something. That something is its base. A payslip has three of them, and they are three different sums of the same lines: Gross: what the contract pays. It is the number on the job offer and on the top of the payslip. Contribution base: the part of the pay that social security takes its percentage of. Often the gross; sometimes less (capped, or without exempt items). Taxable base: the part of the pay the withholding tax is computed on. Usually the gross, minus the employee contributions (most countries do not tax money you never received), plus benefits in kind (pay you received, but not in cash). The two questions of the previous sections decide, line by line, which base each payslip line enters. Marie's October payslip shows all three cases: Payslip line Amount (€) Gross Contribution base Taxable base Salary 7,500.00 ✓ ✓ ✓ Company car (benefit in kind, never paid in cash) 148.57 – – ✓ Employee contributions 13.07 % −980.25 – – ✓ lowers it The base 7,500.00 7,500.00 6,668.32 What is computed on it the contract contributions: 7,500.00 × 13.07 % = 980.25 withholding tax: 1,770.92 Read the last two rows: the contributions are computed first, on the contribution base; only then is the taxable base known, because it needs the contributions. That is why a payslip has an order, and why "the salary" means three different numbers to HR, to social security and to the tax office. Jurgen pays 1.08 € on 2,300.00 €. Same law, same 13.07 % rate. Some countries shape contributions with a cap; Belgium has none and uses reductions instead. Both are variations on one small model.

p: Chapter 3 · Contributions: employee and employer
x: A social contribution (social security contribution, social charge, national insurance; some countries say payroll tax) is a compulsory payment, computed on pay, that finances social insurance: pensions, health care, unemployment, family benefits. Unlike income tax, it is tied to the job and usually paid by both sides: an employee share, deducted from the gross, and an employer share, paid on top of it. Three things follow from that definition: It is computed per period, on the pay of that period. No yearly estimate, no settlement afterwards, unlike withholding (Chapter 4). It buys rights. Pensions and benefits are often computed from the pay declared for contributions, so a wrong base can cost the employee later, not only the fund now. Each fund is a small formula. A base, a rate, and sometimes a floor, a cap and a reduction: the next section takes it apart.

p: Chapter 3 · Contributions: employee and employer
x: A contribution is a percentage of the pay, with two limits. Take one imaginary fund with round numbers: 10 % of gross pay, with a minimum base of 500 and a maximum base of 5,000 a month, and three employees. Illustrative fund: 10 % of gross, base at least 500 and at most 5,000. Left: what each employee pays. Right: the same amount as a share of their pay. The rate applies in the middle band. Ben earns 3,000 and pays 3,000 × 10 % = 300. The floor is a minimum base: below it, the fund charges as if the pay were 500. Ana earns 300 and still pays 50, that is 16.7 % of her pay. Some funds use a minimum contribution instead. The cap is a maximum base: above it, nothing more is due. Cleo earns 8,000 and pays 500, only 6.25 % of her pay. A cap makes a contribution regressive: the higher the pay, the smaller the share. Reductions. Some laws then subtract a reduction, for low wages or for target groups; Jurgen's case below. Contribution = min( max(base, floor), cap ) × rate − reductions Every country's contributions are a combination of these knobs: Knob Question Variants Base which earnings count? gross; basic only; basic + housing Rate how much, for whom? one per fund; by side, nationality or sector Floor minimum base or amount? none; a minimum contribution Cap a ceiling? none; per month; per year to date; tiers Who pays employee, employer, both? employer only for accident funds Reductions who pays less? low wages; first hires; target groups Around the world United States: Social Security has a yearly cap tracked year to date; Medicare has none. India: provident fund on basic salary; state insurance only below a wage threshold. Saudi Arabia: on basic + housing; the employee share only for nationals. Mexico: on an integrated daily wage, capped at 25 × a legal reference unit. Kenya: pension in two tiers between a lower and an upper limit.

p: Chapter 4 · Withholding tax
x: A yearly tax, collected in instalments: five ways to do it Explain withholding as an advance on a yearly income tax, and name the main withholding methods Compute a progressive tax slice by slice Run an annualisation formula by hand, for a single employee and for a married one Tell the marginal rate from the effective rate, and find the low-wage trap Explain why bonuses and other irregular pay need their own tax method Mélanie's withholding tax for October 2026 is 826.70 €. It is not "the tax on 4,000 €": it is one twelfth of a yearly tax, computed as if she earned this salary every month. Another country would look at what she earned since January, read a table, or not withhold at all. Knowing which road a country takes explains almost every rule in its tax module.

p: Chapter 4 · Withholding tax
x: Income tax is a tax on a person's income for a whole year. In most countries the employee does not pay it in one go at the end of the year. Instead, the employer deducts a part of it from every payslip and pays that part to the tax office on the employee's behalf. That deduction is the withholding tax (also called pay-as-you-earn, PAYE, or tax at source). Three things follow from that definition: It is the employee's tax, not the employer's. It comes out of the gross, like the employee contributions. The employer is only a collector: it deducts, declares and pays. It is an estimate. On the payslip, the employer does not know the employee's whole year: other income, a second job, a partner's income, deductible expenses. So each instalment is a best guess. The real tax comes later. After the year, the tax office computes the real tax on everything and settles the difference: a refund, or a bill to the employee. Illustrative numbers. The employer withholds 300 a month, 3,600 over the year. The real tax, computed after the year, is 3,400: the tax office refunds 200 to the employee. Had the real tax been higher, the employee would pay the difference.

p: Chapter 4 · Withholding tax
x: So every localization answers one question: how do you turn a yearly tax into a monthly instalment? Countries pick one of five methods. 1 · Annualise one period HowTax this month's pay as if it came every month of the year, then divide the yearly tax by the number of periods. WhereBelgium, US federal, Egypt, Pakistan Corrects? No: the final assessment settles the year. 2 · Cumulative HowTax the income since the start of the year (or projected for the year), minus the tax already withheld. WhereIndia, Turkey, Poland Corrects? Yes, every period. 3 · Period tables HowRead the tax from an official table made for the pay frequency (month, week…). WhereMexico, the Netherlands Corrects?Only as far as the table is designed to. 4 · None HowNo income tax on salaries, so nothing to withhold. WhereUAE, Saudi Arabia Corrects?Nothing to correct. 5 · Employee files himself HowThe employer withholds nothing and only reports the salaries; the tax office collects from the employee. WhereHong Kong Corrects?Nothing to correct on the payslip. The method shapes the code. An annualising country needs only this month's lines; a cumulative one needs every earlier payslip of the tax year, including a previous employer's. Around the world India: cumulative; actual months plus projected months give the annual tax, spread over the months left. Mexico: tax tables per pay frequency, plus an employment subsidy. United States: annualise per period with the employee's W-4, then a second layer of state tax. Australia: period pay converted to weekly, put through coefficients (a × x − b), converted back. Hong Kong: no withholding; each employee pays his own tax.

p: Chapter 4 · Withholding tax
x: Most income taxes are progressive: each slice of income is taxed at its own band's rate. Belgium's 2026 scale:3 Annual net taxable (€) Tax 0.01 – 16,710.00 26.75 % 16,710.01 – 29,500.00 4,469.93 + 42.80 % above 16,710 29,500.01 – 51,050.00 9,944.05 + 48.15 % above 29,500 above 51,050.00 20,320.38 + 53.50 % above 51,050 The fixed amounts are the tax on all slices below each band, precomputed so a rule looks up one row. Around the world Netherlands: monthly brackets, the annual table divided by 12, with separate tables for residents and non-residents. Kenya: monthly bands, then fixed reliefs subtracted (personal relief, insurance, housing levy). Morocco: one monthly table where each bracket has a rate and a fixed deduction, the same shortcut as Belgium's fixed amounts. Turkey, Poland: the bands apply to the income since 1 January, so an employee climbs into a higher band during the year. Lithuania: one flat rate, but the tax-free amount shrinks as income rises, which makes the tax progressive anyway. Common pitfall "Mélanie is in the 48.15 % band, so her tax is 48.15 %." Only the slice above 29,500 € is. Her withholding is 20.67 % of her gross.7

x: Partial months, absences, and what an hour is worth Prorate a monthly salary with the common methods and explain why they differ Compute a mid-month joiner's first payslip, and test thresholds on a full-month equivalent Classify absences as paid by the employer, paid by a fund, or unpaid Compute an hourly rate and an overtime premium Describe how Odoo turns time into payslip lines Yannick joins MyVidangeCompany on Thursday 12 March 2026 at 3,600.00 € a month. How much does he earn for March? Four payroll teams, four answers: 2,270.77 €, 2,290.91 €, 2,322.58 € or 2,326.15 €. All four are defensible. This chapter is about choosing a denominator, and about everything else that turns time into money.

p: Chapter 5 · Time, proration and overtime
x: A monthly salary pays for a full month. When the employee is paid for only part of it (he joins or leaves mid-month, or takes unpaid days), the payroll pays the same share of the salary. That is proration (pro rata, prorating, partial-period pay): Prorated salary = Monthly salary × paid time ÷ time in the period The paid time is the part of the period the employer pays for: days worked, plus paid days off such as public holidays or paid leave. Three things follow from that definition: Time only matters when the month is incomplete. A monthly employee gets the same salary every full month, whatever the number of days in it. The denominator is a choice. Working days, calendar days, a fixed 30 days: each gives a different amount for the same absence. Every absence needs an answer to "who pays?" A paid day stays in the paid time; an unpaid day leaves it, and a day paid by a fund leaves the payslip too. Illustrative numbers: 3,000 a month, 20 working days in the month, the working-days method. A joiner on day 6 is paid 15 days; two unpaid days cost 2/20 of the salary.

p: Chapter 5 · Time, proration and overtime
x: Three inputs decide how time becomes money: The work schedule: hours per day, days per week. The cast works 38 hours, Monday to Friday (UNVERIFIED as the sector's working time). Public holidays: paid days off. Belgium has ten.2 The pay basis: monthly, or hourly and daily, where every hour or day worked is paid.

p: Chapter 5 · Time, proration and overtime
h: Proration: the denominator is a policy
x: March 2026: 22 working days. Yannick is under contract for 14 of them (and 20 of the 31 calendar days). Method Formula Yannick, March 2026 Working days 3,600.00 × 14 / 22 2,290.91 Calendar days 3,600.00 × 20 / 31 2,322.58 Fixed daily rate × days worked 3,600.00 × 3/13 ÷ 5 × 14 2,326.15 Full month − missing days at a fixed daily rate 3,600.00 − 3,600.00 × 3/13 ÷ 5 × 8 2,270.77 The same contract and the same start date give four March salaries. The "fixed daily rate" is a Belgian convention: a week is worth monthly × 3/13 (a quarter has 3 months and 13 weeks), a day a fifth of that.3 Other countries use a 30-day month, 30.4 days, or a 12-month average. Key idea Proration is a ratio, and the denominator is a policy. Belgian law sets no method for a monthly employee's incomplete month (UNVERIFIED: practice, not law). Choose one, write it down, and use it for joiners, leavers and unpaid days alike. Around the world Saudi Arabia: real calendar days or a fixed 30-day month. Switzerland: a company option for the 30-day method. Mexico: 30.4 days per month for tax. Hong Kong: leave pay uses the average daily wage of the last 12 months. Philippines: a daily wage on the contract, converted between pay frequencies.

p: Chapter 5 · Time, proration and overtime
x: Overtime is time above a daily or weekly limit, paid at a premium and often taxed specially. Overtime pay = hours × hourly rate × (100 % + premium) The hourly rate is again a convention; in Belgium, monthly × 3 / 13 / weekly hours. Belgian law sets a premium of at least 50 % (100 % on Sundays and holidays).1 Worked example: Jurgen, 4 hours at 150 % Line Amount (€) Hourly rate 2,300.00 × 3 / 13 / 38 13.97 Overtime 4 h × 13.97 × 150 % 83.82 The hourly-rate convention is common practice, UNVERIFIED as a legal rule.5 Odoo pays 83.81 €: it does not round the hourly rate first.6 Around the world Switzerland: 125 %, 150 % or 200 %. Morocco: 25 %, 50 % or 100 %. United States: 150 % as a work entry; a federal deduction for overtime, capped year to date. UAE: weekday and rest-day overtime, each at its work-entry rate. Kenya, Netherlands, India: no overtime rule in the module. In Belgium Some overtime hours are free of contributions or carry a tax reduction, but only up to a yearly number of hours.7,8 The same four hours can be treated three ways, so the payroll needs an hour counter per employee and year.

p: Chapter 5 · Time, proration and overtime
x: Every payroll system, Odoo included, turns time into money in four moves. Illustrative month: 3,000 a month, 20 working days, of which 17 worked, a public holiday, a sick day paid by the employer and an unpaid day. 1What is knownThe work schedule: which days and hours are expected. The public holidays. The approved time off. → 2Each day gets a type one colour per type, as in step 3; the type says who pays the day → 3One line per type Worked · 17 days · paid Public holiday · 1 · paid Sick · 1 · paid Unpaid · 1 · not paid → 4Rules turn it into moneySalary = 3,000 × 19 paid days ÷ 20 2,850contributions and tax are then computed on it In Odoo. Work entries are generated from the employee's version (hr.version), its calendar and the time off, then summed into hr.payslip.worked_days lines, one per work entry type; the type says whether the day is paid. p: Chapter 5 · Time, proration and overtime
x: A monthly employee earns the same salary every full month; time matters for joiners, leavers, absences and overtime. Proration's denominator is a policy: Yannick's March is 2,270.77 € to 2,326.15 € depending on the method. Thresholds tested on monthly pay must use a full-month equivalent, or every joiner looks like a low earner. Every absence is paid by the employer, paid by a fund, or unpaid. An unpaid day lowers Jurgen's net from 2,143.05 € to 2,075.34 €; a short sick day leaves his gross unchanged. Overtime = hours × hourly rate × (1 + premium); the hourly rate is also a convention. p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
x: Bonuses, holiday pay, mistakes, and the last payslip Recognise the patterns behind irregular pay: 13th months and bonuses, holiday pay, accruals and provisions Choose a correction method, and know why some errors cannot be recovered from the employee Apply a garnishment ceiling on net pay Tell notice, payment in lieu of notice, severance and end-of-service gratuity apart Assemble a leaver's final pay from its components On 31 October 2026 MyVidangeCompany dismisses Emma after seven years, with immediate effect and an indemnity in lieu of notice. Her last pay is the biggest of her career: 48,959.75 € gross, five different components, three different tax rates, and 25,311.63 € net. None of it follows the monthly formula of Chapters 2 to 4. This chapter covers the pay that does not come every month: bonuses, holiday pay, corrections and leavers.

p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
x: Irregular pay (non-recurring pay, one-off payments; tax laws often say non-periodic income) is any pay that does not come with every regular payslip: a 13th month, a bonus, a holiday bonus, a correction of an earlier month. A leaver's final pay (final settlement, full and final settlement) is the last pay of a contract. It collects several irregular items at once: the last salary, the bonus and leave earned but not yet paid, and money for the end of the contract itself. Three things follow from that definition: It does not fit the monthly formula. Annualise a double month and the employee looks like a high earner for a year. Irregular pay usually gets its own tax method (Chapter 4) and often its own payslip. It is earned before it is paid. A 13th month is earned month by month; a leaver is owed the share earned so far. A final pay is a list of items. The items are the same everywhere; the law of each country says which are due (see Leavers below). Illustrative numbers, 3,000 a month. Left: an employee who stays gets a holiday bonus in June and a 13th month in December. Right: one who leaves at the end of September gets, in one month, the last salary, 9/12 of the 13th month, the untaken leave and the notice paid in lieu: more than five normal months.

p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
x: Many countries add a payment once or twice a year: a 13th month, a Christmas bonus, a religious-holiday allowance. They share three design questions: Question Options When is it paid? once a year; in two halves; pro rata at exit How is it accrued? not at all; or a monthly provision, so the cost lands in the month it was earned How is it taxed? its own method, not the monthly formula (Chapter 4) In Odoo, such a payment is usually a separate payslip on its own structure, with its own rules and tax method, rather than an extra line on the monthly payslip. Around the world Mexico: the Christmas bonus has its own structure, an exempt part and monthly provisions. Philippines: a 13th-month provision every month. Switzerland: 13th and 14th month, with provisions. Luxembourg: separate structures with a tax rule for non-periodic income. Indonesia: the religious-holiday allowance, entered as a payslip input.

x: MyVidangeCompany's sector agreement grants a year-end premium of one monthly salary in December. It carries ordinary contributions, a flat tax rate (Chapter 4), and pushes up the quarterly special contribution (Chapter 3). p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
x: Paid leave is the employee's right to a number of days off a year, set by law or contract, without losing pay. Holiday pay is the money tied to those days. It comes in up to three forms, and each one lands on a different payslip: The salary continues The employee is on leave; the salary keeps running as if he worked. When the month of the days off Payslip same gross; the days show as paid leave instead of worked (Chapter 5) Where almost everywhere A holiday bonus Extra money on top of the salary, so the employee can afford the holiday. When once a year, often before summer Payslip an extra amount, often its own payslip and tax method Where Belgium, Mexico, Australia (leave loading) Untaken leave paid out Days earned but not taken when the contract ends become money. When the final pay Payslip days left × daily rate, one line of the final pay Where Saudi Arabia, UAE, Belgium In a few systems a fund pays the holiday money instead of the employer (Belgian blue-collar workers); then it never appears on the payslip.

p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
x: Belgian white-collar employees get a holiday bonus of 92 % of a monthly salary, earned in the previous year. Instead of ordinary contributions, a special 13.07 % deduction applies to part of it, and it is taxed at a flat rate.2,4 Worked example: Mélanie's holiday bonus, June 2026 Line Amount (€) Holiday bonus 92 % × 4,000.00 3,680.00 Special 13.07 % on 85 % of the salary (3,400.00) −444.38 Taxable 3,235.62 Withholding, holiday-pay rate 42.39 % −1,371.58 Net holiday bonus 1,864.04 Odoo's June payslip gives the same special deduction, withholding and net.1 In Belgium Three variants: simple (the salary during the days off), double (the 92 % bonus) and exit holiday pay, which settles both when a contract ends.3 The 85 % base is practice, not a legal figure (UNVERIFIED).

p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
x: A correction fixes a payslip that was computed with wrong or late information: an unpaid day reported after the payroll ran, a raise signed late, a wrong rate. It happens whenever the error is found, often weeks later. What it means for the payslip depends on how far the payslip has already travelled: before the bank transfer nothing has left the company; after it, the money and the declarations have, and only the difference can still be settled. 1Computed, not paid yetFix the data, cancel and recompute.Nothing has left the company, so nothing needs undoing. → 2Paid, small error, same yearAdjust on the next payslip: one extra line for the difference, plus or minus.The declared month stays wrong until its return is corrected. → 3Large, or an earlier yearRefund and reissue: a negative copy cancels the original, a new payslip replaces it.More documents; the declarations must be amended. The further the payslip went (paid, declared, a closed year), the heavier the fix. The law adds limits: some deductions cannot be recovered from the employee later (in Belgium, a contribution not withheld in time),6 a closed tax year needs a special form, and arrears have their own tax rule.7 Worked example: Jurgen's forgotten unpaid day Jurgen's October unpaid day is entered after October was paid. MyVidangeCompany deducts the 106.15 € (Chapter 5's daily rate) on the November payslip, and November's reduction, withholding and special contribution follow the lower gross. October's line in the quarterly return is corrected when it is filed. When deductions exceed earnings, the net goes negative and a bank cannot pay it. The usual policy is to pay zero and carry the rest forward; the Belgian structure has a NET_TO_RECOVER line for that. Around the world India, Turkey, Poland: the cumulative method corrects itself next month. Egypt, Pakistan: a year-to-date tax adjustment wizard adds a correction line. Australia: a pay-event report already sent can be replaced in full. Philippines: a year-end annualisation trues up the year. In Odoo. A validated payslip can be refunded: a negated copy linked to the original. Chapter 15 corrects a payslip after validation.

p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
x: A court can order the employer to pay part of the salary to a creditor. Almost every country protects a minimum: only the net above legal thresholds can be seized, in slices. In Belgium nothing below 1,419.00 € of net can be seized in 2026, then growing slices; on Mélanie's 2,614.26 €, at most 906.46 €.8,9 In Odoo. A garnishment is a payslip adjustment (hr.salary.attachment); the rule applies the legal ceiling.

p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
x: A leaver is an employee whose contract ends: he resigns, is dismissed, reaches the end of a fixed-term contract, or retires. It happens on a known last day, often after a notice period. For the payroll, the leaver's last pay, the final pay, must settle everything still owed in one go: there is no next month to fix a forgotten item. The items fall into three groups: What goes into a final pay Earned before the end Last salary, prorated Bonus earned so far (9/12 of a 13th month) Leave not taken Owed whatever the reason for leaving. Because of the end Notice paid in lieu Severance pay or end-of-service gratuity Depends on who ended the contract, and why. Taken back, and paperwork Recoveries: advances, equipment Exit notice, certificates for the employee A deduction or a document, not pay. The law of each country decides which items are due, and how each one is taxed. Four terms are often confused: Term What it is Typical formula Notice a period between announcement and end, worked and paid as usual length by seniority Payment in lieu of notice the notice not worked, paid at once weekly pay × weeks of notice Severance pay compensation for losing the job, on top of notice an amount per year of service End-of-service gratuity earned through the years, paid at any exit a share of salary per year, accrued monthly Around the world Saudi Arabia, UAE: end-of-service gratuity, accrued monthly, paid when a departure reason is set. India: a monthly gratuity line; "full-and-final" payslips on departure. Hong Kong: severance reduced by the employer's provident-fund contributions. Australia: lump sums with tax-free limits by years of service. Turkey: severance pay with a legal ceiling.

p: Chapter 6 · Irregular pay, corrections and leavers
h: Case study: Emma, dismissed with an indemnity in lieu of notice
x: Emma's notice depends on her seniority: 7 years and 1 month gives 24 weeks.10 MyVidangeCompany pays them as an indemnity, valued on her annual pay, benefits included: Indemnity = (12 × monthly + year-end premium + holiday bonus) ÷ 52 × weeks of notice For Emma: (60,000.00 + 5,000.00 + 4,600.00) ÷ 52 × 24 = 32,123.08 €. It carries ordinary contributions11 and is taxed on a separate indemnity scale (38.96 % for Emma). Common pitfall Getting the hire date wrong by one month. Counted from 1 November 2019, Emma's 24 weeks become 21: 4,015.39 € less. Check the contract start, earlier contracts with the same employer, and the notice start before computing. In Belgium Notice grows with seniority by steps (3 more weeks per started year from 5 years), with a cap for recent contracts. An employee who resigns has a shorter notice. The employer also pays a special contribution of 1 % to 3 % on dismissal indemnities (UNVERIFIED band; the calculator applies 1 %).12

p: Chapter 7 · Declarations and the compliance calendar
x: Who gets which report, how often, and what must match Name the four kinds of payroll filing every country has, and the newer per-payslip and per-pay-run models Explain why every declaration is a sum or a list of validated payslip lines Say which filings must agree with each other Place filings, payments and yearly events on one calendar Name the Odoo models that produce each of MyVidangeCompany's filings Payroll does not end at the bank transfer. MyVidangeCompany notifies each hire before the first hour, reports the tax withheld every month, the contributions every quarter, and each employee's yearly totals every February. All must agree with the payslips and with each other. The form names are Belgian; the four kinds of filing exist almost everywhere.

p: Chapter 7 · Declarations and the compliance calendar
x: A payroll declaration (payroll return, filing, payroll report) is a report the employer sends to an authority about its payroll: who works for it, what they earned, and what was withheld or is owed. Most declarations come with a payment, or are checked against one. They go to the social security office, the tax authority, and sometimes the employee. Three things follow from that definition: It is built from the payslips. Every declaration is a filtered sum or list of validated payslip lines. If a declaration needs a number the payslips do not have, the payslips are missing a rule. It runs on the authority's calendar, not the payroll's: at each hire or exit, each month or quarter, each year (the four clocks of Chapter 1). Declarations must agree with each other and with the payments. An authority that receives two numbers compares them. Illustrative numbers, three employees. The tax return adds up the tax withheld on the three payslips and comes with the payment. The contribution return lists each employee's base and contributions. Nothing in either return is typed by hand.

p: Chapter 7 · Declarations and the compliance calendar
x: Three parties receive payroll reports, and each needs them for a different reason. Social security must know who is insured and on what pay: it collects the contributions, and it computes each worker's pension, unemployment and sick pay from what the employer declared. The tax authority collects the tax withheld, which is the employee's income tax paid in advance, and must credit it to the right person. The employee needs his yearly totals to file his own tax return. Who receives what, and why Social security Hire and exit notices Contribution return, per worker To collect the contributions and to compute each worker's rights. Tax authority Withholding return, with the payment Annual certificate per employee To collect the tax withheld and credit it to each employee. Employee The payslip, every period A copy of his annual certificate To check his pay and file his own tax return. All of them are built from the same validated payslips.

h: The quarterly social security return and the annual tax slip
x: The quarterly return (DmfA) lists, per worker, the pay by code, working time, contributions and reductions; it is due on the last day of the month after the quarter.2 Each February, the employer sends one annual tax slip (281.10) per employee to the tax administration, with a copy to the employee.7

p: Chapter 7 · Declarations and the compliance calendar
x: An authority often receives the same money twice, by two different roads, and compares the two. Withholding tax is the clearest case: Every month, the withholding return gives the month's total for all employees, and the employer pays it. The tax office knows what it received. After the year, the annual certificates give each employee's total for the year. The tax office knows how much to credit to each person against his final tax. Both are sums of the same payslip lines, one by month and one by employee, so their grand totals must be equal. If the certificates add up to more than the returns, employees are credited with tax that nobody paid, and the tax office asks why. Tax withheld Jan Feb … Dec Annual certificate Employee A 300 300 … 300 3,600 Employee B 200 200 … 200 2,400 Employee C, joins in July 0 0 … 100 600 Monthly return 500 500 … 600 6,600 = 6,600 Illustrative numbers. Each column total is a monthly return; each row total is an annual certificate. The twelve returns (6 × 500 + 6 × 600) and the three certificates (3,600 + 2,400 + 600) must both come to 6,600. Contributions follow the same logic: the contribution return lists each worker's contributions, and their sum must equal what was paid for the period. Both must also equal the payroll debts in the accounts (Chapter 8). At MyVidangeCompany, the twelve monthly withholding returns of 2026 must add up to the annual tax slips, and each quarterly return must match the contributions paid. A localization makes these matches true by construction: every filing reads the same validated lines. Common pitfall Filing from a PDF or a spreadsheet. A payslip corrected after filing leaves the return silently out of date. Generate each declaration from the validated lines and regenerate it after a correction.

h: The payslip and the records to keep
x: Every country also sets the content of the payslip and the records to keep. In Belgium the payslip must show how pay is computed, and the employer keeps an individual account per worker.8,9 Retention periods were not researched (UNVERIFIED). A localization covers them with the payslip report and a yearly per-employee report.

p: Chapter 7 · Declarations and the compliance calendar
x: Put together, the filings give a calendar with four rhythms: the event, the month, the quarter and the year (Chapter 1). Worked example: MyVidangeCompany's fourth quarter 2026 Date Event 1 Nov new withholding formula 2 Nov exit notice for Emma early Nov October net pay transferred: 37,177.22 € 13 Nov withholding return and payment for October: 20,580.61 € December year-end premiums 31 Jan 2027 quarterly social security return for Q4 28 Feb 2027 annual tax slips for 2026 In practice Order the filings by the cost of being late: the hire notice first, then the withholding return, then the contribution return, then the annual certificates. If a payroll bureau keeps filing one, agree how Odoo's numbers reach it. In Odoo. Each localization adds one model per filing: Belgium has l10n_be.dmfa, l10n_be.274_xx and l10n_be.281_xx, among others. The yearly per-employee ones share hr.payroll.declaration.mixin (Chapter 22). p: Chapter 7 · Declarations and the compliance calendar
x: Declarations are sums or lists of validated payslip lines; design the lines first. Four kinds of filing exist almost everywhere: hire and exit notification, periodic contribution return, periodic withholding return, annual employee certificate. Some countries report every payslip (Mexico) or every pay run (Australia); some add payment-control files (the UAE's Wage Protection System). p: Chapter 8 · Accounting for payroll
x: One payslip, one balanced entry, and liabilities that wait to be paid Build the journal entry of a payslip: costs on one side, liabilities on the other Explain why employee deductions are liabilities, and only the employer charges add cost Follow MyVidangeCompany's October 2026 through T-accounts until every liability is paid Explain provisions for holiday pay, 13th months and gratuities Describe how Odoo creates the entry and the payment file At month end the accountant wants one thing from payroll: a journal entry. The salary and the employer's charges are costs. Everything withheld is money owed to someone else until it is paid. Payroll accounting is mostly the story of those debts. The shape is the same in every country; only the account numbers change.

p: Chapter 8 · Accounting for payroll
x: Payroll accounting (payroll bookkeeping, booking the payroll) records the pay run in the company's books. Each period it posts one balanced journal entry: the cost of the period on the debit side, and on the credit side what the company now owes, and to whom. Later payments close those debts one by one. Three things follow from that definition: The cost is the employer cost. Gross wages plus the employer's own charges; nothing withheld from the employee adds to it. Withheld money is a debt, not a cost. Until it is paid, the tax and contributions kept back sit on liability accounts, like the net pay not yet transferred. The entry is a sum of payslip lines. Each salary rule says which account it goes to; the entry adds them up. Illustrative numbers: the payslip of Chapter 2's figure (1,000 gross, 200 employer contributions). 1,200 of cost on the debit side; on the credit side, 650 owed to the employee, 350 to social security and 200 to the tax authority.

p: Chapter 8 · Accounting for payroll
h: From book to bank: the T-accounts
x: Accountants follow each account with a T-account: the account drawn as a large T, its name on top. Amounts that increase the account go on one side, amounts that decrease it on the other, and the difference between the two sides, the balance, is what the account holds. For a debt such as net pay due, the right side (credit) records what the company comes to owe and the left side (debit) what it pays off, so the balance is what is still owed. Take account 455, the net pay MyVidangeCompany owes its employees for October 2026: 455 Net pay due Debit (paid off) Transfer, early Nov14,917.31 Credit (now owed) Payroll entry, 31 Oct14,917.31 Balance: still owed0.00 After the payroll entry14,917.31 owed ↓ the bank pays the employees After the salary transfer0.00 owed The payroll entry fills the account; the bank payment empties it, and books the same amount as money leaving the bank account (550). The three other debts of the entry work the same way, each emptied on its own date: Account Emptied by When 453 Tax withheld, 4,646.49 € payment with the withholding return by 13 November 454 Social security, 8,065.22 € monthly advances, then the balance balance by 31 January 440 Voucher issuer, 220.00 € payment of its invoice on the invoice terms A balance left on a payroll liability after its due date is the first thing an accountant checks: a payment that did not happen, or a line booked on the wrong account. Common pitfall Booking the employee contributions and the withholding as expenses. They are liabilities; the cost is already in the gross wages. Booking them as expenses counts them twice.

p: Chapter 8 · Accounting for payroll
x: A provision is a debt the company records before the bill arrives: it knows it will have to pay an amount later, so it books the cost now, a little each month. Take a 13th month of 1,200, earned over the year and paid in December (illustrative numbers, contributions left out): Month Cost booked Provision (owed so far) Cash paid January 100 100 0 February 100 200 0 … … … … December, before payment 100 1,200 0 December, payment 0 0 1,200 Without the provision, December would carry 1,200 of cost and the other months none. With it, each month carries its share, and the December payment simply pays off the debt already recorded. Each month: debit provision cost / credit provision liability. On payment: debit provision liability / credit net pay due Saudi Arabia and the UAE provision the gratuity, Mexico and the Philippines the bonuses (Chapter 6). Many Belgian employers provision holiday pay (account 625 against 456), an accounting policy the book does not compute.

p: Chapter 8 · Accounting for payroll
x: The net pay leaves the company as one bank file with a line per employee; the legal payment date applies (Chapter 1).3 Tax and contributions are paid separately, each with its own reference.4 MyVidangeCompany uses a SEPA credit-transfer file. Around the world Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg: SEPA credit transfer. United States: a NACHA (ACH) file. Australia: an ABA bank file. UAE, Saudi Arabia: a Wage Protection System salary file, checked by the labour ministry. India: a payment advice and a bank e-NET file. In Odoo. hr_payroll_account gives each salary rule an account_debit and account_credit, and each structure a journal; each localization's _account module sets them for its chart. At validation Odoo builds the entry from the lines and groups them by account. If they do not balance (a rule without an account), Odoo adds an Adjustment Entry line instead of refusing: the entry posts and looks fine, and it is wrong. hr_payroll_account_iso20022 exports the SEPA file. Chapter 16 posts and pays February 2026. In practice Before go-live, validate one payslip per structure and read each entry against the chart of accounts. Agree the accounts with the accountant before the first pay run; changing them later means reversing entries.

p: Chapter 8 · Accounting for payroll
x: A payslip becomes one balanced entry: costs (gross wages, employer contributions, other personnel costs) against liabilities (net pay, social security, tax withheld, third parties). Employee deductions are liabilities held for third parties; only employer charges add cost. MyVidangeCompany's October 2026: 27,849.02 € on each side. Each liability is closed by a payment on its own date. A benefit in kind moves no money and has no line in the entry. Pay earned monthly but paid later (holiday pay, 13th month, gratuity) is provisioned each month. Odoo books the entry at validation from the accounts on the salary rules, and balances any gap with an Adjustment Entry line that you should treat as a bug. p: Chapter 9 · What varies between countries, and what doesn't
x: Every payroll fact lives in one of four layers. The question to ask is: who decides this value, and how often does it change? Employee HR, per person · changes at hire, raise, family event, exit e.g. wage, family situation, company carhr.version fields Company The employer or its accountant · changes rarely e.g. pay frequency, sector agreement, bank and journalssettings, company fields Country The legislator, then the localization team · changes yearly, sometimes mid-year e.g. contribution rates, tax scale, declarationsl10n_xx_hr_payroll Framework Odoo R&D · changes with each release e.g. payslips, the rule engine, dated parameters, pay runshr_payroll Each layer is built on the one below it: a company configures what its country's module allows, and an employee's values fill fields the country declared. p: Chapter 9 · What varies between countries, and what doesn't

Days not worked, paid leave and overtime change the amount, each at its own rate. Framework piecework entries and worked daysChapters 5, 14 2 · Totals feed the formulas A contribution or a tax is a percentage of a total of payslip lines: the gross, the contribution base, the taxable base. Framework piecesalary rule categoriesChapters 2, 20 3 · Rates change over time Every year brings new rates and tax scales, but an old payslip must keep the rates of its own period. Framework piecedated rule parametersChapters 11, 21 4 · Every period ends in an entry and a payment The pay run is booked in the accounts and the net is paid to the bank, every period, the same way. Framework piecepay runs and payroll accountingChapters 8, 16 5 · The authorities want reports What was paid and withheld is reported to the tax office and social security, monthly, quarterly or yearly. p: Chapter 10 · Researching a new country
x: A test needs an expected value. If that value comes from Odoo itself, the test only proves that Odoo agrees with Odoo. A golden payslip is a payslip whose every line was computed outside Odoo, from the law, by something that does not share Odoo's code. When Odoo's payslip matches it line by line, the localization is right for that case; when it does not, one of the two is wrong, and you know exactly which line to look at. How to get one: 1Build a calculatorA spreadsheet or a small script, written from the law and the research template. No Odoo code. → 2Prove itIt must reproduce the administration's own worked examples, to the cent.The book's Belgian script matched the tax office's simulator first. → 3Compute the castRun it for a few employees that cover the cases: low and high pay, a joiner, a leaver. → 4Compare with OdooSame employees, same month in Odoo. Compare line by line, then freeze the expected lines in a test. Same amount: the line is right. It becomes a test that protects it from future changes. Different amount: find the cause. Odoo has a bug, the calculator has one, or the law is unclear: a question for the expert. Worked example: Mélanie and Marie, calculator against Odoo Line Mélanie, calculator Mélanie, Odoo Marie, calculator Marie, Odoo Gross salary 4,000.00 4,000.00 7,500.00 7,500.00 Employee social security 522.80 522.80 980.25 980.25 Car benefit in kind — — 148.57 151.42 Taxable salary 3,477.20 3,477.20 6,668.32 6,671.17 Withholding tax 826.70 826.69 1,770.92 1,750.15 Net 2,614.26 2,614.27 4,663.91 4,684.68 October 2026 payslips.4,5 Where both agree, the payslip is correct. Where they differ, find the cause and take it to the expert: Odoo rounds the monthly tax down where the official formula rounds half up (Mélanie's cent),1 spreads the car benefit by days (Chapter 2), and deducts a transport exemption (Chapter 4). Common pitfall Generating the "expected" values by running Odoo and pasting the output into the test. That test can never fail for a wrong rule, only for a changed one. The first snapshot of each case must be checked against an independent source (Chapter 21). Around the world MX: tests write the hand computation in a comment next to each expected value. US: the FIT rule quotes the tax office's worksheet in its comments. BE: JSON snapshots hold the expected lines of large payslips. NL: no test reaches the upper tax bands.

p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time
x: Effective dates, indexation, yearly tables, reference units, mid-year and retroactive changes, downloaded rates, and the dated parameter that absorbs them Model any legal value as a timeline of effective dates Tell indexation of wages (employee data) from a new table or unit (country data) Say which parameter value Odoo uses for a payslip, and why the period end decides Handle a scheduled reform, a mid-year change, and a law that applies to the past Choose between typing rates into data files and downloading them from the administration Every country changes its payroll law on its own calendar. p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time
h: Every legal value is a timeline
x: A rate is never "13.07 %". It is "13.07 % from a date, until a later value replaces it". The law changes on several rhythms: Rhythm Example What the module stores Yearly tables and units MX tax tables each 1 January, reference unit each 1 February one new value per year Wage indexation BE sector wages +2.21 % on 1 Jan 20263 a new version of each contract Scheduled reform MX employer pension rates loaded up to 2030 future values, loaded in advance Mid-year change AU super on 1 Jul; BE withholding on 1 Nov 2026 a dated value, sometimes a rule branch Retroactive change BE overtime reduction published in July, in force from 1 Jan a past-dated value, plus corrections Key idea Store every legal value with its start date, and never edit a value that has already been used. A new law is a new dated record. Then every payslip, old or new, recomputes with the law of its own period. 1 Jan 2026: MX tax tables, MX minimum wage, BE scale and index → 1 Feb: MX reference unit → 1 Jul: AU super basis → 1 Aug: BE notice table → 1 Nov: BE second tax formula of the year (and in July, a BE decree reaching back to 1 Jan).

p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time
h: Indexation: a new wage, not a new parameter
x: Some countries raise wages automatically with prices. The percentage is law; the result is a new wage for each person. Worked example: Mélanie on 1 January 2026 Belgian sector wages rose by 2.21 % on 1 January 2026.3 Mélanie's 2025 salary of 3,913.51 € became 4,000.00 €.4 Before 1 Jan 2026 From 1 Jan 2026 Mélanie's monthly salary 3,913.51 4,000.00 Index factor × 1.0221 Indexation is a law about every employee's wage, so its result is employee data. Odoo stores it as a new version of the contract, not as a rule parameter. Version until 31 Dec 20253,913.51 € New version from 1 Jan 20264,000.00 € December 2025 payslip reads 3,913.51 January 2026 payslip reads 4,000.00 In Odoo. The Salary Increase wizard (hr.payroll.salary.increase, Chapter 13) takes employees, a date and a rate. It does not change the old version: it adds one per employee, starting on the indexation date. Each payslip then picks the version valid in its period, so December keeps the old wage and January gets the new one. If January was already validated when the indexation is entered, the wizard opens the correction wizard (Chapter 15).

p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time
h: Yearly tables: one dated value per year
x: Most countries reissue their tax tables every year. The design is the same everywhere: one parameter, one value per year, the same shape every year (a list of brackets, or a dict of lists by frequency in Mexico). The Belgian value for 2026: <record id="rule_parameter_value_prp_basic_bareme_2026" model="hr.rule.parameter.value"> <field name="parameter_value">[(16710.0, 0.2675), (29500.0, 0.428), (51050.0, 0.4815), (None, 0.535)]</field> <field name="rule_parameter_id" ref="rule_parameter_prp_basic_bareme"/> <field name="date_from" eval="datetime(2026, 1, 1).date()"/> </record> Its bands match the official formula (16,710 / 29,500 / 51,050).2 That check, value by value against the source, is the yearly upkeep of a localization (Chapter 22). Common pitfall Editing last year's value to this year's bands "because it is January". Every recomputed payslip of last year (a correction, a year-end certificate, a test) then silently uses this year's law. Add a record; never overwrite history.

p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time
h: How Odoo picks the value for a payslip
x: A salary rule asks for a parameter by its code. It never mentions a date. # in a rule or a helper on hr.payslip uma = payslip._rule_parameter('l10n_mx_uma')['daily'] The engine returns the latest value whose date_from is on or before the payslip's end date (date_to). Two consequences for the law: a value starting on the 16th applies to the whole period, and a value has no end date, so a temporary measure is two values (the measure, and the one restoring the baseline). Chapter 21 shows how a rule reads it. Worked example: Jurgen, July and August 2026 A Belgian tax reduction for low wages rises on 1 August 2026. Jurgen's July payslip reads the old value, his August payslip the new one.4 July 2026 August 2026 Withholding before the reduction 294.95 294.95 Low-wage tax reduction −132.63 −150.62 Withholding 162.32 144.33 Net pay 2,125.06 2,143.05 The demo database agrees: the August pay run withholds 17.99 € less than July, exactly 150.62 − 132.63.5 The parameter behind that reduction, in Configuration > Rule Parameters. ① its code, the only thing the rule knows. ② a value already loaded for 2028. ③ the value from 1 August 2026 that Jurgen's August payslip reads. ④ the older value his July payslip reads. Common pitfall Assuming the work period is what the law looks at. Many texts speak of income paid from a date: a July salary paid on 3 August gets the July value in Odoo. If the payment date decides, the rule must pass it as reference date.

p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time
x: A mid-year change of a number is another dated value. A change of method needs code, and the question is how to keep that code dated. Around the world: Australia, 1 July 2026 Superannuation moves to a new base with a year-to-date cap. The parameter changes shape (a number before, a dict after) and the rule branches on a date in its code: rule = payslip._rule_parameter("l10n_au_withholding_super") if payslip.date_from >= date(2026, 7, 1): prior_slips = payslip._l10n_au_get_year_to_date_slips() prior_ote = prior_slips._get_line_values(['QE'], compute_sum=True)['QE']['sum']['total'] remaining = max(rule['cap'] - prior_ote, 0) result = min(categories['QE'], remaining) * rule['rate'] / 100 else: result = categories['OTE'] * (rule / 100) But the date now lives in two places, and the rule keys on date_from while the lookup keys on date_to. A weekly payslip from 29 June to 5 July reads the new dict but takes the old branch, which divides a dict by 100 (read from the code, not run: UNVERIFIED). Branching on the parameter's own shape keeps one source of truth. Worked example: Marie's November rise (Belgium) The 1 November 2026 formula (Chapter 4) changed three family levers: Marie's withholding rises by 28.86 €, the singles' falls by 8.47 €.1 In Odoo it needs no code: three new records dated 1 November, next to the January ones. <record id="rule_parameter_value_prp_max_spouse_income_2026_11" model="hr.rule.parameter.value"> <field name="parameter_value">11780.0</field> <field name="rule_parameter_id" ref="rule_parameter_prp_max_spouse_income"/> <field name="date_from" eval="datetime(2026, 11, 1).date()"/> </record> In practice On 8 October 2026 master had no value dated 1 November for those parameters: Marie would be under-withheld by 28.86 € a month. The weekly payroll data cron (Chapter 21) delivers the fix without a module upgrade, if it is merged before the November pay runs. Track announced changes with their dates.

p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time
x: Sometimes the law is published after its start date. A Belgian decree of 24 July 2026 extended an overtime tax reduction to all sectors from 1 January 2026.1 Start of the rule in the past → Publication → Data update value dated at the start → Computed with the old rule → New and recomputed payslips see the new rule → Correction payslips (Chapter 6, Chapter 15) A past-dated value fixes new and recomputed payslips. Validated ones record what was paid; the difference becomes a correction. Odoo flags validated payslips when a version, the company settings or the time off change after validation, but not when a rule parameter gets a past-dated value: find those payslips yourself. Common pitfall Assuming the system will "catch up" after a retroactive value. It won't. List the validated payslips of the period, recompute them in a correction run, and check whether filed declarations need an amendment.

p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time

Tests load fixed copies instead. Also, a corrected file for a past period updates that value in place: an intended exception to "never edit history".

p: Chapter 11 · Laws that change over time
x: Every legal value is a timeline. Countries change values yearly (tables, units), quarterly, mid-year, on a multi-year schedule, and sometimes retroactively. Indexation changes the wage, so it is a new hr.version (wizard Salary Increase); a new rate, table or unit is a new hr.rule.parameter.value. Store a reference unit plus multipliers: one value a year moves every cap. A payslip reads the latest value whose date_from is on or before its date_to; a temporary measure needs a closing value. A change of number is data; a change of method needs code, and the date should live in one place. A retroactive value fixes new and recomputed payslips; validated ones are corrected, and nothing flags them for you. Rates published as files or APIs can be imported into dated parameters (BE, CH) or fields (SA); payslips stay reproducible. p: Chapter 12 · Tour and setup
x: Four Odoo objects decide how a payslip is computed: the structure type, the structure, the salary rule and the rule parameter. Their names sound alike and everyone mixes them up at first. The easiest way to keep them apart is to follow one payslip and ask: how does Odoo know what to compute for Mélanie in October? Mélanie's version (her contract terms) says: pay category CP200 BE 1Structure type · CP200 BEwhat kind of pay: monthly, fixed wage 2Structure · Monthly Pay (BE)the regular monthly payslip · the type's default 3Rule BASICbasic salary 3Rule ONSSsocial security 3Rule P.Pwithholding tax … 213 rules Double holiday pay 13th month Termination fees other structures of the same type, for special payslips 4Rule parametera shelf of dated numbers, outside any structure Professional expenses cap2025: 5,9302026: 6,070 ← the withholding rules read it by its code, at the payslip's date Read the figure in order of the numbers: The structure type is the kind of pay. It is stored on the employee's version and answers who is paid how, and how often: here, a monthly fixed wage under the sector agreement CP 200. Change an employee's type and a different set of rules runs, without touching a single rule. A structure is the recipe for one kind of payslip. The type has a default structure for the regular monthly payslip, and others for payslips that have their own tax treatment: double holiday pay, the 13th month, termination fees. Each runs on its own payslip (Chapters 15 and 17). A salary rule computes one line of the payslip: when it applies (its condition), how much (its formula) and which totals it feeds (its categories). The regular Belgian structure has 213 of them; P.P computes the withholding tax. A rule parameter holds a legal number with its dates. A rule never writes the law's numbers in its code: the withholding rules ask for the parameter by its code, and get the value valid on the payslip's date, 6,070 in 2026. Next year's law is a new value, not a new rule (Chapters 11 and 21). Key idea Each object changes for a different reason: the type when the employee's kind of pay changes, a structure when a new kind of payslip is needed, a rule when the calculation method changes, a parameter when the law's numbers change. Keeping them apart is what lets a yearly law change be a one-line data update. Configuration > Salary > Structures > Monthly Pay (BE). ① the structure name. ② the Salary Rules tab, with the rules and their categories. ③ the BASIC rule. The header holds the type (CP200 BE), Use Worked Day Lines (this structure is driven by time), the scheduled pay and the salary journal. Configuration > Salary > Rule Parameters, the notice length after a dismissal: ① its code, which rules use to read it, ② the value valid from 1 August and ③ the value valid from 1 January 2020. A payslip reads the value in force at its end date (Chapters 11 and 21). Around the world Belgium, UAE, Saudi Arabia: monthly structure types. Philippines: a semi-monthly type. Hong Kong: an extra weekly type for casual employees. India: a second type for interns. Belgium, Luxembourg: several structures per type, because holiday pay, bonuses and termination are separate payslips.

Choosing the employer's sector agreement (the joint committee, CP 200 for most office employees) in Company data activates the ones that apply. p: Chapter 13 · Employees and versions
x: The employee holds the person (identity, family, bank); the version holds the agreed terms (wage, schedule, pay category, benefits). A version starts on its effective date and ends the day before the next one; a contract is the run of versions sharing the same contract dates. A payslip reads every version of the same contract active in its period; a new contract means a separate payslip. The wage is an amount per pay period; the pay frequency comes from the structure type. Benefits are version fields read by rules; one-off amounts are payslip inputs; recurring deductions with a balance are payslip adjustments. Hire with the contract start date, raise with a new version, and read the dashboard after each.

p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
h: Time: schedules, time off, worked days
x: How a calendar and a leave request become paid and unpaid days on a payslip Read a working schedule and compute the hours of a month from it Explain what a time type is and which of its fields change pay Follow time off and public holidays into generated work entries, then into worked-days lines Explain how a localization values an absence, with Jurgen's April as the example Record sick days, unpaid days, leave and overtime so that the payslip is right without typing a number Jurgen was ill on 14 April and took an unpaid day on 24 April; April also has Easter Monday. They come from his schedule (what he was expected to work), his time off (what he did not) and the time types that say how each hour is paid.

p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
x: A monthly salary is not paid "for the month": Odoo pays it day by day, according to what each day was. This chapter follows one month, Jurgen's April 2026, through the three steps below. 1What Odoo knows Working scheduleMonday to Friday, 7.6 hours a day Public holidaysEaster Monday, 6 April Approved time offsick on 14 April unpaid day on 24 April → 2One work entry per working day Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri 1 2 3 6 7 8 9 10 13 14 15 16 17 20 21 22 23 24 27 28 29 30 worked public holiday sick unpaid computed when needed, never stored → 3Worked days on the payslip Attendance19 days · 1,981.54 Public holiday1 day · 106.15 Sick1 day · 106.15 Unpaid1 day · 0.00 Basic salary2,193.84 What Odoo knows. The working schedule says which days and hours were expected. Public holidays and approved time off say what happened instead. Work entries. For each expected day, Odoo derives one work entry with a time type: worked, public holiday, sick, unpaid. Nobody types them, and they are not stored: Odoo computes them again whenever a payslip needs them, so a late change of time off is never forgotten. Worked days. The payslip groups the entries by type into worked-days lines. Each type says whether it is paid, so the unpaid day is worth 0, and the total of the lines is the basic salary. The rules then compute everything else from it.

p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
x: A working schedule (resource.calendar) lists the weekly attendance slots. It says which hours were expected, and is the denominator when a wage is cut into hours. MyVidangeCompany's Standard 38 hours/week runs Monday to Friday, 8:00–12:00 and 12:30–16:06: 7.6 hours a day, so 167.2 expected hours in April 2026 (22 weekdays, Easter Monday included). Public holidays are closure days: leaves of the whole company, with the time type Public Holiday.

p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
x: Every hour of the month has a kind: worked, sick, holiday, unpaid. A time type (hr.work.entry.type) names that kind and says how it is paid. Time off types and schedules point to it, and each worked-days line of the payslip is one time type. p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
x: Payroll only uses the result of the Time Off app: an approved request becomes a leave on the employee's calendar, with its time type. Paid leave consumes an allocation (20 days a year at MyVidangeCompany); sick and unpaid days do not. The payroll status of a leave (payslip_state) protects validated months. A leave approved after its month was validated is blocked: a dashboard card says Time Off missing from period's payslip, the Deferred Time Off responsible (Chapter 12) is warned, and you correct that month's payslip (Mission 15.2).

p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
h: Work entries are generated, not stored
x: A work entry is "this employee, this day, this time type, this many hours". Odoo does not store them: hr.version generates them whenever a payslip needs its worked days. Mon 13 Tue 14 Wed 15 Thu 16 Fri 17 1The schedule expects 7.6 h 7.6 h 7.6 h 7.6 h 7.6 h 2Approved time off sick, full day 3Work entries Attendance 7.6 h Sick 7.6 h Attendance 7.6 h Attendance 7.6 h Attendance 7.6 h One week of Jurgen's April. Odoo starts from what the schedule expects (1), lays the approved time off and public holidays over it (2), and what remains is attendance (3). Each day gets one entry per kind of time, with its hours. An absence counts the scheduled hours, not the clock: a full sick day on a 38-hour week is 7.6 hours. Overlaps have a winner. A public holiday beats a personal leave on the same day, unless the localization lists the leave as taking precedence (in Belgium: long sickness, parental leave, unpaid…). Because nothing is stored, a draft payslip always follows today's data. Only validated payslips are frozen.

p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
h: From work entries to worked days
x: The payslip groups the entries by time type, converts hours to days with the schedule, and writes one worked-days line (hr.payslip.worked_days) per type, with an amount. Jurgen, April 2026, Worked Days tab. ① the sick day: 1 day, 7 h 36 min, paid 106.15 €. ② the unpaid day: 1 day, 0.00 €. ③ Easter Monday, paid 106.15 €. Attendance shows 19 days and 1,981.54 €. The total is 22 days and 2,193.84 €, which becomes the basic salary. Line Days Hours Amount (€) WORK100 Attendance 19 144.4 1,981.54 LEAVE110 Sick Time Off 1 7.6 106.15 LEAVE90 Unpaid 1 7.6 0.00 LEAVE500 Public Holiday 1 7.6 106.15 Basic salary 22 167.2 2,193.84 The generic engine values each line at wage ÷ hours of the month × hours × pay rate. A localization may replace that convention. The Belgian one values every non-attendance line at a fixed hourly rate and gives attendance the rest of the wage, so one missing day always costs the same. In Belgium The fixed hourly rate is wage × 3 ÷ (13 × weekly hours): 2,300 × 3 ÷ (13 × 38) = 13.97 € for Jurgen, so 7.6 hours are worth 106.15 € and his basic salary is 2,300.00 − 106.16 = 2,193.84 €. Chapter 5 compares the proration methods. Yannick's March works the same way: the 8 days before his start become an unpaid OUT line (Out of Contract).

p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
h: Overtime is a time type too
x: Overtime is a working-time type with a pay rate above 100 %, here Voluntary Overtime (150%) (VOLOT150), entered as a time off request of that type. It reads oddly, but it is the same mechanism. Jurgen, May 2026 (demo database, before any raise). ① 4 hours of voluntary overtime at 150 %: 0 days, 4 h, 83.81 €. The line feeds the salary rule VOLOT150, which adds it to gross pay. The request behind the overtime line, approved. ① type Voluntary Overtime (150%). ② 20 May 2026, 4:30 PM → 8:30 PM. ③ duration 4 h: the type is counted in hours, so the form asks for a start and an end time. Around the world Belgium: 143 time types, because each absence has its own social security code. Philippines: 50 (night shifts, rest days, holiday premiums). Australia, Switzerland: 31 and 25. United States: 12. Netherlands, India, France: about 10 each. In practice: fix time at the source If a worked-days line is wrong, fix the leave, the schedule or the version and refresh the draft. A hand-edited line stops Odoo from recomputing the worked days, so later changes will not reach it.

p: Chapter 14 · Time: schedules, time off, worked days
x: The schedule says which hours were expected; MyVidangeCompany's has 7.6 hours a day, 167.2 hours in April 2026. A time type is the single record behind leave types, schedule slots and worked-days lines; its code, pay rate and categories decide the money. Approved time off and public holidays become leaves on the calendar; a leave that arrives after its month was validated is blocked until the payslip is corrected. Work entries are generated on demand and never stored; absences count scheduled hours; overlaps follow a precedence. Worked-days lines carry days, hours and amounts; a localization decides how absences are valued (Belgium: a fixed 3/13 hourly rate). Fix time at its source and refresh the draft; never hand-edit a worked-days amount.

p: Chapter 15 · Pay runs and payslips
x: Generate, compute, review, validate, and correct without breaking the audit trail Follow a pay run through its states and say what each button does Read a payslip tab by tab: worked days, inputs, computation, other info Use warnings to decide whether a run can be validated Pick the right tool for a mistake: recompute, cancel, correct, or an off-cycle payslip Run January to May 2026 for MyVidangeCompany, including a late correction and overtime End of January 2026: four employees, no payslip yet, and the bank wants a file by the 28th. This chapter is the monthly routine: open a pay run, let Odoo build the payslips, review, validate, and correct a payslip after it was validated.

p: Chapter 15 · Pay runs and payslips
x: A pay run (hr.payslip.run) is one batch of payslips: everyone paid on the same structure for the same period, for example Monthly Pay, February 2026. You work on the run instead of on fifty payslips one by one. You never set a run's status yourself. It follows its payslips, and tells you at a glance where the month stands: Draftsome employees have no payslip yet → Readyevery employee has a payslip; some are still drafts → Doneevery payslip is validated → Paidevery payslip is paid (If every payslip is cancelled, the run is Cancelled.) Payslips > Pay Runs on the full demo database. ① the October run is Done: validated, not paid yet. ② the January run is Paid. ③ Pay opens the payment wizard (Chapter 16). ④ Total Cost, the employer cost of the run. When you create a run, Odoo finds the valid versions (running in the period, on the structure's pay category, not already paid in another regular run) and creates one draft payslip per version, with its worked days (Chapter 14). The salary lines come with Compute. The February 2026 run, one row per payslip. ① Marie's payslip. The footer sums the run: 23,246.73 € total cost, 18,800.00 € basic wage.

p: Chapter 15 · Pay runs and payslips
x: A payslip has four tabs, in the order of the calculation: Worked Days (Chapter 14), Salary Inputs (values typed for this payslip, or brought by adjustments), Salary Computation (the lines the rules computed, hr.payslip.line) and Other Info (accounting date, journal). Mélanie, February 2026, Salary Computation. ① basic salary 4,000.00 €. ② employee social security, 13.07 % of 4,000.00. ③ taxable salary. ④ withholding tax. ⑤ special social security contribution. ⑥ net salary 2,614.27 €.
